evidence.requirements: Most of the brief is met. The list has the heading, name links, family, L3, Search, the Family select and the '<n> cartridges' count (index.html:13-32, app.js:15-29); `7,62 x 51` finds 308 Win. through norm() (format.js:39-41). The detail view has the metadata, water capacity with its source link (app.js:47-58), tables grouped by section with Symbol/Value/Unit columns and the tolerance on the value's row (format.js:29-36; screenshot detail-308_win shows 'L1 39.62 -0.2'). It has the Print button, the 'All cartridges' link and a bookmarkable hash route (app.js:72-88). The SVG is at 1 unit = 1 mm with an aria-label, a dash-dot centre line, a hatched section and a title block with the scale (drawing.js:381-403). Every required dimension is drawn, and missing values are reported in notes (drawing.js:145-216). Partly met: (1) Print does not put the drawing at full width. It is capped at 105 mm high (style.css:76), so in print-308_win.jpg it fills only about half the page width and the bottom third of the page is empty. (2) The α dimension is not tied to the shoulder in a readable way. Its arc sits between the neck corner and the cone apex, inside the neck and bullet, and its label hangs on a long extension line (drawing.js:313-352). On 9,3 x 74 R it lands over the bullet nose. (3) No spec, plan or other process artefacts were delivered, although the brief's Process section asks for a spec phase.
evidence.correctness: The geometry follows the rules closely. Rim type uses 1.05 and 0.98 (drawing.js:24-29). The chamfer uses min(f·tanβ, R1/4) (drawing.js:142). The rimfire half-round has radius min(R/2,(R1-P1)/2) (drawing.js:132-139). The groove floor and ramp, and the belted ramp at δ ((R3-E1)/2/tanδ) then the belt to E and a step in, are right (drawing.js:161-169); the belt shows in detail-300_win_mag. The shoulder fillets use r1 min and r2 (drawing.js:189-190). The seating and k factors split by pistol and rifle (drawing.js:68-80). The tangent-ogive radius and centre and the ellipse, cone and SWC meplats follow the rule (drawing.js:94-107). The heeled bullet uses H2 outside and H2-2tb for the heel (drawing.js:89-92; detail-22_long_rifle shows the heel). Walls tn/tb, w and the pocket tables are right (drawing.js:198-222). The 44 Mag bullet base measures about 26.07 mm in the screenshot, which matches L3 - 0.6·G1. Proportions agree with reference/308_win, 300_win_mag, 9_mm_luger and 22_long_rifle. Values and angles are formatted as published ('10°58'0"', '4150'), and the print test checks one A4 page for all 25 records (e2e.test.js:84-92). Weak points: the α construction is placed inside the neck. Diameter dimension lines run straight through the section view. Straight cases get an invented wall taper from tb to tn between w and the seating depth (drawing.js:225-229). Angle rows show the degree sign twice, as '40°' in Value and '°' in Unit.
evidence.security: Every data string goes through esc() before innerHTML (app.js:6, 11, 34-66; drawing.js:21, 376, 394, 399). There is no eval, Function or setTimeout with a string. The page makes no network requests, and the e2e test asserts this (e2e.test.js:19). The only external URL is the user-clicked source link with rel=noopener noreferrer. The only inline script is a tiny onsubmit="return false" (index.html:14).
evidence.code_quality: There are three small modules: format, drawing and app. The UMD wrappers let Node tests load them (format.js:2-5, drawing.js:3-6). The geometry steps follow the brief's rule numbers. drawing.js is dense: draw() runs about 165 lines with very long one-liners such as drawing.js:230 and 290. There is a garbled comment at drawing.js:9 ('title block font size // monospace character width'). Constants are kept in sync with the CSS only by comments (drawing.js:13-14, style.css:76). Error handling is reasonable: a missing route shows 'Cartridge not found' (app.js:83).
evidence.tests: Unit tests check the rim-type thresholds, chamfer, groove, belt ramp at δ, rimmed step, rimfire half-round, straight versus bottleneck, tn/tb/w/pocket, seating, meplat, heeled bullet, missing-value notes, the required label ids, and label-to-label and label-to-outline collisions for all 25 records (unit.test.js:47-188). The e2e tests in Playwright over file:// cover search, family filter, count, routing with reload, tolerance placement, label overlap and viewBox bounds in the browser, one-page PDF print for every record, and no network requests (e2e.test.js). Not covered: the ogive and ellipse shapes beyond the tip, α placement, dark mode, phone width, and print content and legibility.
evidence.ux_design: The tables are dense and calm, with right-aligned tabular numbers and muted units (detail-308_win). Labels never overlap, thanks to the staircase rows. But label and title-block text have a fixed size in mm, so on short cases they dwarf the part. In detail-9_mm_luger and detail-22_long_rifle the labels are about 45 px tall and the title block takes about a third of the drawing panel. The α arc and its extension lines clutter the neck (detail-308_win, detail-300_win_mag). On 9,3 x 74 R the α leader sits over the bullet nose (detail-9_3_x_74_r). The print layout is clean black on white, but the drawing is only about half width (print-308_win). No dark-mode screenshot was available, though dark variables exist (style.css:8-13).
evidence.accessibility: The SVG has role=img with aria-label and title '<name> drawing' (drawing.js:401-402). Form controls are wrapped in labels, the count has role=status, tables have captions and scope=row headers (app.js:34-36), html has lang=en, and :focus-visible outlines are set (style.css:24). Muted text #5d6670 on #f7f7f5 passes AA contrast. Gaps: focus is not moved to the new h1 on hash navigation, even though tabindex=-1 is set (app.js:60, 85). The drawing's text alternative is only its name. The 'No cartridge matches.' message is not announced.
evidence.simplicity: There are no runtime dependencies, and Playwright is the only dev dependency. The whole app is about 600 lines of plain JS, CSS and HTML, which fits the problem. There is no build step, and data.js is loaded as a script so the app works from file://.
evidence.maintainability: There is no README, no docs, no ADRs, no specs and no CI configuration. Nothing says how to run the app or the tests, or that the e2e suite needs Playwright browsers installed. There is no versioning or changelog and no Node version pin (no engines field or .nvmrc), although the lockfile pins playwright 1.64.1. The test scripts in package.json and the regression suites are the main help to a newcomer. Design choices, such as the tapered straight-case wall, the α construction and the 105 mm print cap, are recorded only in code comments.
evidence.visual_design: The page uses restrained system typography, a monospace face for the drawing, a beige case and copper bullet on the outside view, and blue dimensions. The hatching is crisp. The list and tables look finished and consistent across pages. The drawing's scale is inconsistent: label size relative to the part varies between cartridges, and on pistol and rimfire pages the oversized bold title block looks unbalanced (detail-9_mm_luger, detail-44_rem_mag). The scale line 'Scale 1.34 : 1 (A4 print)' does not describe what the screen shows.
evidence.layout: On the list page the heading, controls and count come first, with no overflow (list.jpg). The detail page runs title and toolbar, then a metadata grid, the drawing, and four-column table grids, which is a sound hierarchy. Inside the drawing panel, a large part of the space goes to the title block and empty area under the dimensions, so the table grid starts well below the fold. In print the tables fill four columns neatly, but the drawing is narrow and about 30% of the page is blank at the bottom (print-308_win). Nothing is clipped or overlapping in any screenshot.
evidence.usability: Finding a cartridge takes one step with live search, which tolerates decimal commas and spacing and also searches alternative names. The detail view opens in one click, and both Print and the back link are visible at the top right. Addresses can be bookmarked. Small gaps: the count reads '1 cartridges', the Search field has no hint, and there is no screenshot evidence for phone width.
evidence.reception: Reloaders and engineers would trust the complete, faithfully formatted C.I.P. tables and the one-page printout. The drawing is accurate to scale but looks less professional than the OpenBallistics references: oversized labels on small cases, an unconventional α callout inside the neck, and a title block that dominates. Many would use it as a reference, but it is not yet polished enough to recommend without reservation.

unmet_requirements: Printed detail view does not show the drawing at full width: it is limited by max-height 105 mm and covers about half the page width (style.css:76, print-308_win.jpg)

The α shoulder-angle dimension is drawn inside the neck and bullet, with a detached label; on shallow shoulders (9,3 x 74 R) it lands over the bullet nose, so it does not clearly label the shoulder (drawing.js:313-352)
No spec, plan or other process artefacts were delivered for the brief's required spec/plan/review phases
strengths: The geometry implements the brief's rules faithfully: chamfer, groove, belt ramp at δ, rimfire half-round, filleted shoulder, tangent ogive, ellipse and cone noses, the heeled 22 LR bullet, walls, solid head and primer pocket. Proportions match the reference drawings.
Data is shown exactly as published, with tolerances on the value's row, angles in D°M'S" form, escaped HTML and no network access. It works from file:// with hash routes that can be bookmarked.
Good automated checks: unit tests for each drawing rule, plus Playwright tests over all 25 records for label overlap, viewBox bounds, one-page A4 print and no network requests.
issues: Drawing legibility and proportion: label and title-block text have a fixed size in mm, so on short cases (9 mm Luger, 22 LR) the labels are huge and the title block takes a third of the panel. In print the drawing is only half width.
The α dimension is drawn unconventionally inside the neck and bullet with a detached leader, sitting over the bullet nose on 9,3 x 74 R. Diameter dimension lines run through the section view.
Maintainability: there is no README, CI, docs/ADRs/specs, versioning or Node version pin; run and test instructions exist only implicitly in package.json.
review.verdict: The app is a small, dependency-free, carefully tested implementation whose geometry and data presentation follow the brief closely and print on one A4 page for every record. It is not ready to publish: label and title-block scaling, α placement and print use of space need refinement, and it has no README or CI.
